title: Seborrheic dermatitis and androgenetic alopecia: a scalp-homeostasis framework
headline: A fresh review argues the two scalp conditions overlap (SD in 40-50% of AGA patients) and should be managed by restoring scalp barrier and microbiome balance together; it is a framework, not a product or a trial.
evidenceTier: Narrative review (abstract read) + small cross-sectional study (abstract read); no intervention evidence
fit: Relevant only if scalp flaking or thinning is a concern. It supports a barrier-and-inflammation-first approach to scalp care, but it does not test one.
displaces: Fits nowhere as a product. If acted on, it would change how a scalp routine is judged (barrier and inflammation before stimulating actives), not add a step.
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
summaryPoints: Review abstract (read): SD is present in 40-50% of AGA patients; shared factors proposed include androgen-driven sebum, microbial imbalance, barrier dysfunction and inflammatory signalling. The authors call for combined, individualized management.

Cross-sectional study (abstract read): in 34 adults with scalp SD, severity correlated with triglycerides and liver enzymes (GGT rho 0.745). Associational, tiny, European setting; it does not show cause and I would not act on it.
Neither abstract reports skin or hair type; scalp conditions in tightly coiled, high-porosity hair were not addressed. Full text not read for either.
fitLine: Useful lens for scalp care; no tested action.

fitAxes.why: The review names barrier dysfunction as a shared factor (abstract).
